items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: But that was the first time I'd heard George Shearing.

ctx.x: I'm happy that I did it, because these were the last days of 52nd Street. And we played 52nd Street, and then we played Baltimore, we played Detroit, Chicago, Cleveland, and a few other places I don't remember. We spent most of the Fall of 1947 on the road.

In December 1947, we went back to New York and we played somewhere there... Oh, we played a place called the Royal Roost, which was on Broadway. During that time, we got an engagement to play... What's the other hall, other than Carnegie...? Anyway, I can't think of the name of the hall now. But it's a very popular hall in New York. And they had this concert there featuring Billy Eckstine and me as his accompanist. If I remember, on this particular concert was a blind pianist that had just arrived in the United…

And that was the last engagement that I played with Billy, because by this time, the money had really not gotten any better. I was still making this $100 a week, and I was really, literally starving to death! Anyway, the promising thing was supposed to have been an engagement in Chicago that
